title: Multi-agent orchestration
summary: Agent roles compiled to each host's native agent format, with parallel isolation by worktree, a concurrency limit, human escalation and a handoff contract.

questions.prompt: Which agent roles does the project delegate to?

options.label: Planner, explorer, implementer, reviewer, tester
options.tradeoff: Every routing class gets its own role; more definitions to maintain and more handoffs.

options.label: Implementer and reviewer
options.tradeoff: Fewest roles that still separate writing from verifying; exploration and planning stay with the main agent.

options.label: None
options.tradeoff: No definitions and no handoffs; no per-role routing and no independent review.

questions.prompt: What may the reviewer change? (Only the role's access is set here; what a review step must pass is the review bar of the verification-gate pack.)

options.label: Nothing: findings only
options.tradeoff: Independent verdict; fixes cost an extra handoff back to the implementer.

options.label: Trivial fixes (typos, formatting)
options.tradeoff: Saves handoffs on nits; the reviewer's independence is slightly weaker.

options.label: Anything
options.tradeoff: Fastest to done; the reviewer marks its own work and independence is lost.

options.label: A git worktree per task
options.tradeoff: Agents cannot overwrite each other; one checkout and one cold build per task.

options.label: Branches in one working tree
options.tradeoff: One checkout; tasks must run one at a time.

options.label: None
options.tradeoff: No setup; parallel agents can clobber each other.

options.label: ../<repo>-wt/<slug>
options.tradeoff: Outside the repo, so tools never index them; one more directory next to the repo.

options.label: .worktrees/ inside the repo (gitignored)
options.tradeoff: Easy to find; editors and search may index them.

options.label: Wherever the host agent puts them
options.tradeoff: Nothing to configure; the location differs per host and `go-getter worktree new` is not used.

questions.prompt: How many agents may run at once?

options.label: 1 agent
options.tradeoff: No merge conflicts or cold caches; no parallel work.

options.label: 3 agents
options.tradeoff: Some parallelism; each extra agent adds a cold cache and a merge to resolve.

options.label: 5 agents
options.tradeoff: More parallel plan steps; more merges to resolve and more spend at once.

options.label: 10 agents
options.tradeoff: The most parallel work; needs worktree isolation, per-step budgets and conflict-aware scheduling to stay cheap.

questions.prompt: When must an agent hand over to a human?

options.label: When blocked, before irreversible or outward-facing actions, and on a guardrail denial
options.tradeoff: Catches the costly mistakes; a few confirmations per task.

options.label: Only when blocked
options.tradeoff: Fewest interruptions; irreversible actions rely on guardrails alone.

options.label: Also before every commit
options.tradeoff: A person sees every change land; slows autonomous work.

questions.prompt: What is the handoff contract between agents?

options.label: Brief in; result and evidence out
options.tradeoff: Small, checkable handoffs; the delegator must write a proper brief.

options.label: Free-form summary
options.tradeoff: Least friction; results are not checkable and drift in size.

options.label: Structured JSON
options.tradeoff: Machine-checkable; rigid, and models spend tokens on the format.

questions.prompt: How many minutes does an agent's claim on a work unit last before it must be renewed?
How many minutes does a CI job's claim on a work unit last (the job's own time limit)?
How many minutes does a person's claim on a work unit last before it must be renewed?
How many minutes of clock difference between workers and the git host does a lease tolerate?
After how many days without action by its holder or on any child is a parent work unit flagged idle?
How many KB of brief fields may a delegated unit keep in the claims ledger before they spill to the tracker issue?
Among how many of the highest-priority ready work units does a worker pick, by a hash of its id, the one it claims?
How many work units may one worker hold at once (a number, or `max-concurrent` to use the per-worker agent limit)?
How many work units of one feature may be claimed at once across all workers (a number, or `none` for no limit)?

decisions.title: Work is delegated to planner, explorer, implementer, reviewer and tester agents

roles.description: Turns a brief into an ordered plan with a done-when check per step.
roles.instructions: Turn the brief into an ordered plan with a done-when check per step. Read the code and docs you need; do not change files.

roles.description: Searches and reads the codebase to answer questions, with file and line references.
roles.instructions: Search and read the code to answer the brief's questions. Report file paths and line numbers; do not change files.

roles.description: Makes the change a brief describes and runs the project checks.
roles.instructions: Make the change the brief describes, nothing more. Run the project's checks before you report.

roles.description: Reviews a change against the brief, decisions and guardrails and reports findings by severity.
roles.instructions: Review the change against the brief and the project's decisions and guardrails. Report findings by severity, each with file and line; say so when there are none.

roles.description: Writes and runs tests for a change and reports failures with their output.
roles.instructions: Write and run tests for the change. Report failures with the command and its output; do not change production code.

decisions.body:
## Decision

Delegate work to these agent roles: planner (plan), explorer (explore), implementer (implement), reviewer (review), tester (debug); the parenthesis is the routing task class. `go-getter apply` compiles them into each host agent's native format. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Separate roles are the routing lever and keep verification independent of implementation (decisions 0014, 0016).

decisions.body:
## Decision

Delegate work to these agent roles: implementer (implement), reviewer (review); the parenthesis is the routing task class. `go-getter apply` compiles them into each host agent's native format. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Separate roles are the routing lever and keep verification independent of implementation (decisions 0014, 0016).

decisions.title: No agent roles are defined
decisions.body:
## Decision

Do not define agent roles; the main agent works alone (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Separate roles are the routing lever and keep verification independent of implementation (decisions 0014, 0016).

decisions.title: The reviewer reports findings and changes nothing

role-notes.reviewer: Do not modify files; report findings only.

decisions.body:
## Decision

The reviewer agent gets read-only access and reports findings only (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The reviewer's independence is what makes its verdict worth a gate (decision 0013).

guardrails.title: The reviewer must not modify files

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given a findings-only reviewer, a reviewer that edits marks its own work.

enforcement.check: Instruction plus the agent file's tool restriction where the host has one

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

The reviewer reports findings and changes nothing. Hosts with tool lists restrict it natively; elsewhere this is advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: The reviewer may fix trivial issues and reports the rest

role-notes.reviewer: You may fix typos and formatting directly and must list each fix; report everything else as findings.

decisions.body:
## Decision

The reviewer agent may fix typos and formatting directly and reports everything else as findings (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The reviewer's independence is what makes its verdict worth a gate (decision 0013).

guardrails.title: The reviewer may fix only typos and formatting

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given a reviewer allowed trivial fixes, anything larger must go back to the implementer.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

The reviewer fixes only typos and formatting, lists each fix and reports everything else. Advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: The reviewer may change anything

role-notes.reviewer: You may fix the issues you find; list every change you make.

decisions.body:
## Decision

The reviewer agent has full write access (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The reviewer's independence is what makes its verdict worth a gate (decision 0013).

decisions.title: Each parallel task runs in its own git worktree
decisions.body:
## Decision

Run every parallel task in its own git worktree, created with `go-getter worktree new <slug>` (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Parallel agents on one working tree overwrite each other's edits.

guardrails.title: Parallel tasks must each use their own worktree

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given worktree isolation, two agents in one working tree overwrite each other.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Give each parallel task its own worktree (`go-getter worktree new <slug>`). Advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: Each task has its own branch in the single working tree and tasks run one at a time
decisions.body:
## Decision

Give each task its own branch in the single working tree and run tasks one at a time (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Parallel agents on one working tree overwrite each other's edits.

guardrails.title: Tasks sharing a working tree must run one at a time

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given branches in one tree, two agents editing it at once overwrite each other.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Run one task at a time in the working tree, each on its own branch. Advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: Parallel tasks are not isolated
decisions.body:
## Decision

Do not isolate parallel tasks (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Parallel agents on one working tree overwrite each other's edits.

decisions.title: Task worktrees live next to the repository
decisions.body:
## Decision

Create task worktrees in `../<repo>-wt/<slug>` (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A fixed location keeps worktrees discoverable and out of the main tree's way.

decisions.title: Task worktrees live in the gitignored .worktrees directory
decisions.body:
## Decision

Create task worktrees in `.worktrees/<slug>` and keep the directory gitignored (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A fixed location keeps worktrees discoverable and out of the main tree's way.

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given worktrees inside the repo, an unignored directory gets committed as untracked noise.

decisions.title: Task worktrees live wherever the host agent creates them
decisions.body:
## Decision

Let the host agent choose the worktree location; `go-getter worktree new` is not used (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A fixed location keeps worktrees discoverable and out of the main tree's way.

decisions.title: At most {{answer.max-concurrent}} agents run at once
decisions.body:
## Decision

Run at most {{answer.max-concurrent}} agents concurrently; `go-getter worktree new` refuses to exceed it (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Each concurrent agent adds a cold cache and a merge to resolve.

guardrails.title: No more than {{answer.max-concurrent}} agents run at once per worker

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the limit, each extra agent adds a cold cache and a merge.

enforcement.check: Instruction; worktree creation is refused beyond the limit

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Each worker runs at most {{answer.max-concurrent}} agents at once; the limit is per worker, not per project (decision 0169 item 2). `go-getter worktree new` refuses more than that many worktrees. Advisory (tier 1) otherwise.

decisions.title: Agents hand over to a human when blocked, before irreversible or outward-facing actions, and on a guardrail denial

go-getter.escalation: Stop and hand over to a human when blocked, before any irreversible or outward-facing action, and when a guardrail denies an action.

decisions.body:
## Decision

Hand over to a human when blocked, before any irreversible or outward-facing action, and on a guardrail denial (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Agents must stop where a wrong guess is costly or the way forward needs a person (decision 0009).

guardrails.title: Agents must hand over to a human when blocked, before irreversible actions and on a guardrail denial

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the escalation decision, an agent that routes around a denial defeats the guardrail.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Stop and ask a human when blocked, before irreversible or outward-facing actions, and when a guardrail denies an action. Advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: Agents hand over to a human only when blocked

go-getter.escalation: Stop and hand over to a human only when you cannot proceed.

decisions.body:
## Decision

Hand over to a human only when blocked (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Agents must stop where a wrong guess is costly or the way forward needs a person (decision 0009).

guardrails.title: Agents hand over to a human only when blocked

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the escalation decision, agents proceed unless they cannot.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Ask a human only when you cannot proceed. Advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: Agents hand over to a human when blocked, before irreversible actions, on a guardrail denial and before every commit

go-getter.escalation: Stop and hand over to a human when blocked, before any irreversible or outward-facing action, when a guardrail denies an action and before every commit.

decisions.body:
## Decision

Hand over to a human when blocked, before any irreversible or outward-facing action, on a guardrail denial and before every commit (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Agents must stop where a wrong guess is costly or the way forward needs a person (decision 0009).

guardrails.title: Agents must hand over to a human before every commit as well as when blocked or denied

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the escalation decision, a person sees every change before it lands.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Stop and ask a human when blocked, before irreversible or outward-facing actions, on a guardrail denial and before every commit. Advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: Handoffs are a brief in, then a result and evidence out

go-getter.handoff: The brief gives goal, scope and done-when. Reply with the result, then the evidence: commands run with their outcome, and file references.

decisions.body:
## Decision

The delegator sends a brief (goal, scope, done-when); the agent replies with the result, then the evidence (commands run and their outcome, file references) (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A fixed handoff keeps delegated context small and every result checkable (decision 0014).

guardrails.title: Handoffs must carry a brief, a result and evidence

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the contract, a result without evidence cannot be checked and a brief without done-when cannot be verified.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Delegate with goal, scope and done-when; reply with the result and its evidence. Advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: Handoffs are free-form summaries

go-getter.handoff: Reply with a concise summary of what you did and found.

decisions.body:
## Decision

Agents hand over work with a free-form summary (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A fixed handoff keeps delegated context small and every result checkable (decision 0014).

decisions.title: Handoffs are structured JSON objects

go-getter.handoff: Reply with one JSON object: {"status": "done" | "blocked", "summary": string, "files": string[], "evidence": string[]}.

decisions.body:
## Decision

Agents reply with one JSON object: status, summary, files and evidence (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A fixed handoff keeps delegated context small and every result checkable (decision 0014).

guardrails.title: Agent replies must be one JSON object with status, summary, files and evidence

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given structured handoffs, a reply that is not parseable breaks the delegator.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Reply with exactly one JSON object with status, summary, files and evidence. Advisory (tier 1).

decisions.title: The lease of an agent's claim is {{answer.lease-agent}} minutes
decisions.body:
## Decision

The lease of an agent's claim is {{answer.lease-agent}} minutes (decision 0166; pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

An agent that stops without releasing must free its unit soon, and renewal by heartbeat keeps a live agent from losing it; an hour is long enough to ride out a slow step and short enough that a lost agent blocks others for little time.

decisions.title: The lease of a CI job's claim is {{answer.lease-ci}} minutes
decisions.body:
## Decision

The lease of a CI job's claim is {{answer.lease-ci}} minutes (decision 0166; pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A CI job ends by itself, so its lease follows the job's time limit: it frees the unit when the job can no longer be running, with no renewal traffic.

decisions.title: The lease of a person's claim is {{answer.lease-human}} minutes
decisions.body:
## Decision

The lease of a person's claim is {{answer.lease-human}} minutes (decision 0166; pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A person works in long stretches with few commands to renew from, so the lease covers a working day; a shorter one would drop a unit someone is still thinking about.

decisions.title: A lease lapses {{answer.clock-skew}} minutes after its expiry, and a clock that far off the host cannot claim
decisions.body:
## Decision

A lease lapses {{answer.clock-skew}} minutes after its expiry, and a clock that far off the host cannot claim (decision 0166; pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Workers compare their own clocks with a lease expiry, so a margin keeps a small clock difference from taking a live claim; a worker whose clock is off the host by more than the margin could misjudge every lease, so it may not claim.

decisions.title: A parent unit with live children is flagged idle after {{answer.parent-idle}} days without action
decisions.body:
## Decision

A parent unit with live children is flagged idle after {{answer.parent-idle}} days without action (decision 0166; pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A parent with live children holds no lease, so nothing else would show that nobody is working on it; the idle period flags it for a person or K7 to park, and a week keeps a normal pause from raising a flag.

decisions.title: A delegated unit keeps at most {{answer.brief-max}} KB of brief fields in the claims ledger
decisions.body:
## Decision

A delegated unit keeps at most {{answer.brief-max}} KB of brief fields in the claims ledger (decision 0166; pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The ledger is fetched by every claim, so each delegated brief in it must stay small; a brief over the cap is kept on the tracker issue instead, and the ledger holds a pointer to it.

decisions.title: Workers pick among the first {{answer.pick-among}} ready work units
decisions.body:
## Decision

Ready work is ordered by priority, and a worker takes one of the first {{answer.pick-among}} by a hash of its id (decision 0174 item 1). (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Workers asking at the same time spread over several units instead of all contending for the first claim on the ledger (decision 0166 item 1); a larger number spreads more and follows the order less closely.

decisions.title: A worker holds at most {{answer.wip-per-worker}} work units at once
decisions.body:
## Decision

A worker holds at most {{answer.wip-per-worker}} work units at once (`max-concurrent` stands for the agents answer); `go-getter work next` offers it nothing above that (decision 0174 item 2). (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A worker that holds many units finishes none quickly; the default follows the number of agents that may run at once (decision 0156).

decisions.title: At most {{answer.wip-per-feature}} work units of one feature are claimed at once
decisions.body:
## Decision

At most {{answer.wip-per-feature}} work units of one feature are claimed at once (`none` is no limit); `go-getter work next` offers nothing of a feature at its limit (decision 0174 item 2). (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

One feature then cannot take every worker while the others wait; with no limit the order of priority alone decides.
